name: vscode-math
description: Shows code as maths: Σ ∏ ∫ lim, fractions, matrices, piecewise cases, ∀ ∃ and set-builder notation drawn in the editor, plus ≤ ≠ → λ symbols. Python, Julia, JavaScript and TypeScript. Files stay plain text.

commands.title: Math View: Show Notation for This Language

mathView.enabled.description: Show symbols like ≤ and → in place of <= and ->.

mathView.revealOnCursorLine.description: Show the original text on lines that have a cursor or selection, so you never edit hidden characters.

enumDescriptions: Draw maths full size. Lines with big notation (Σ, ∫, fractions, matrices...) are made taller to fit.
Draw maths within a normal line height, with limits beside the Σ.
Leave code as it is; use the hover instead.
mathView.inline.description: Draw maths in the editor on lines without a cursor.

mathView.scale.markdownDescription: How big to draw maths in `tall` mode. Lines with big notation get this much more room: at `1` a line with Σ is 3× the normal height and one with a fraction 2×; at `1.5` they are 4× and 2.5×. Changing it updates the line-height rules for Math View in your `editor.tokenColorCustomizations`.

mathView.hover.description: Show sums like sum(x[i] for i in range(1, n+1)) as typeset math on hover.

mathView.hoverScale.description: Size of the rendered math in hovers.

mathView.symbols.markdownDescription:
Extra symbol substitutions: a JavaScript regex (the key) and the symbol shown in its place. Merged with the built-in ones; set a built-in key to `null` to turn it off. Run **Math View: Show Notation for This Language** to see them all.

Example: `{ "\\*\\*": "^", "!=": null }`

mathView.builtinSymbols.description: Start from the built-in symbol substitutions. Turn off to use only mathView.symbols.

mathView.bigOperators.markdownDescription: Calls written with a generator, like `sum(f(i) for i in range(n))`. A plain LaTeX symbol is drawn with limits under and over (`{ "logsumexp": "\\operatorname{LSE}" }`); a template can use `$body`, `$vars`, `$domain`, `$conds`, `$in` (x ∈ S, cond), `$under` and `$over` (`{ "mean": "\\frac{1}{|$domain|} \\sum_{$in} $body" }`). Merged with the built-ins; `null` removes one. Changing this regenerates the tall-line grammar and asks to reload.

mathView.functions.markdownDescription:
How to draw function calls, as LaTeX templates. `$1`, `$2` are the arguments, `$args` all of them, `$0` the object a method is called on, `$name` a keyword argument, `$1.var`/`$1.body` a lambda's parameters and body, `$2.0` an item of a tuple. Filters: `$1|atom` brackets unless it is a single symbol, `$1|rows` draws a list of lists as matrix rows, `$1|domain` draws `range(n)` as {0, …, n−1}.

Keys: `name`, `name/arity`, `name[keyword]`, `.method`, `.attribute`. A list of templates is tried in order. An object adds options: `{ "template": "...", "height": "tall", "display": false }`.

Example: `{ "softplus": "\\log\\left(1 + e^{$1}\\right)", "hypot/2": "\\sqrt{$1^2 + $2^2}" }`

mathView.identifiers.markdownDescription: Names and constants to draw as LaTeX, e.g. `{ "hbar": "\\hbar" }`. Greek letter names are built in.

mathView.ranges.markdownDescription: Iterables that become the limits of a sum, keyed `name/arity`. `from` and `to` are written in the document's language (not LaTeX) with `$1`, `$2` for the arguments, and get simplified. Example: `{ "np.arange/2": { "from": "$1", "to": "$2 - 1" } }`. Use `set` instead to give LaTeX for the whole domain.

mathView.syntax.markdownDescription: Templates for operators and other syntax: `fraction`, `floorDiv`, `matmul`, `piecewise` (ternaries), `setComprehension`, `listComprehension`, `lambda`, `adjoint`. Set one to `null` to stop drawing it, or give `{ "template": "...", "display": false }` to draw it only inside other maths. Example: `{ "fraction": { "template": "$1 / $2", "display": false } }`.

mathView.nameSuffixes.markdownDescription: Name endings drawn as accents, with `$1` for the rest of the name: `x_hat` → x̂. Built in: `_hat _bar _tilde _vec _dot _ddot _prime _star _inv _T _sq`. Example: `{ "_dag": "$1^{\\dagger}" }`.

mathView.reducers.markdownDescription: JavaScript/TypeScript: which `reduce` operations become which big operator. Keys are an operator (`+`, `*`, `&&`, `||`) or a function such as `max` (matching `Math.max`); values are names in `mathView.bigOperators`. Built in: `{ "+": "sum", "*": "prod", "max": "max", "min": "min", "&&": "all", "||": "any" }`.

mathView.modulePrefixes.markdownDescription: Module names to ignore when looking up notation, so `np.sqrt` uses the `sqrt` entry. Added to the built-ins; start an entry with `-` to remove a built-in one, e.g. `"-torch"`.

mathView.builtinNotation.description: Start from the built-in notation tables. Turn off to use only your own bigOperators, functions, identifiers, ranges and modulePrefixes.
